title: Task, trial and grader
intro: An evaluation task specifies what the agent should accomplish. One execution is a trial. A grader inspects evidence against defined criteria.
takeaway: Evaluate the agent with its harness, tools and environment, not just an isolated model response.

beats.text: A task asks for an authentication fix. Define what success will look like.
Run one trial with the agent system. The system returns a patch and evidence.
A grader inspects the result. It applies the stated success criteria.
The grade describes this one trial. It is not a guarantee about future runs.

title: Check actual behavior
intro: Instead of grading a claim that the bug is fixed, run the changed code on inputs with known expected outcomes.
takeaway: Grade observable results. A good explanation can accompany an incorrect patch.

beats.text: The agent says the bug is fixed. A statement is not the behavior itself.
Run the patch with an empty password. The expected behavior is rejection.
The empty password is rejected. This test has passed.
Record the observed result for grading. Other required cases still need testing.

title: Catch an overbroad fix
intro: Patch A rejects all logins. It fixes the empty-password case but breaks legitimate users. A regression case reveals the overbroad change.
takeaway: A narrow success test can reward the wrong solution. Include behavior that must remain valid.

beats.text: Patch A rejects every login. Both bad and valid passwords fail.
The empty-password case is rejected. That expectation passes.
The valid-password case is also rejected. That expectation fails.
The grader rejects this overbroad fix. Passing one case was insufficient.

title: Repeat trials independently
intro: Repeated trials reveal variation in the agent system. Each should start from the intended clean state so one trial does not contaminate another.
takeaway: Repeated success measures consistency on these tasks. It does not make the system deterministic or prove general safety.

beats.text: Run the same task more than once. Each trial starts in an isolated state.
Trial 1 produces a result. Record the outcome and evidence.
Trial 2 runs from a clean starting point. Its result may differ.
Report the distribution of outcomes. Do not show only the best attempt.

title: Know the grading limits
intro: A suite collects representative tasks. Deterministic tests and model graders cover different properties, and graders themselves need calibration.
takeaway: Passing a suite supports claims within its coverage. Keep held-out cases and inspect grading errors before making broader decisions.

beats.text: Collect tasks that represent real use. Include known failures and valid behavior.
Apply graders suited to each criterion. Some judgments need human calibration.
Inspect false passes and false failures. A flawed grader can reward wrong work.
Use the evidence with stated limits. A passing suite is not automatic release.
